title: Natural coefficient-universe comparison for positive-degree etale cohomology
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact separated scheme and F a quasi-coherent module. Set E=F_et [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module] and let L be sectionwise ULift to coefficient universe u+1. For q=n+1 with n>=0 there exists an additive equivalence H^q(X_et,L(E)) -> H^q(X_et,E), with the small-coefficient group computed using HasExt.standard, commuting with every abelian sheaf endomorphism theta:E->E. The same equivalence works for all theta, and no preservation of injectives by ULift is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03P2, separated-case finite affine open cover argument, naturality on one fixed cover.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover, using quasi-compactness. Separatedness makes its nonempty finite intersections affine. Restricting the tensor sheaf to each intersection gives the tensor sheaf of the pulled-back quasi-coherent module. Ordinary and lifted affine acyclicity kill the positive rows of the two Cech-to-derived spectral sequences, identifying positive-degree cohomology with the homology of the section complexes.

Lift each coefficient endomorphism to its injective resolution. Apply the Cech complex functor termwise to obtain a double-complex morphism commuting with both augmentations. The induced cohomology squares commute. Resolution lifts over the same endomorphism are homotopic, and additive functors send these homotopies to homotopies inducing equal homology maps. Thus both edge identifications intertwine the given sheaf endomorphism, without requiring it to be O-linear or comparing injectives across universes.

In every Cech degree the tuple index set is finite. The maps taking down every lifted section and lifting every small section are inverse additive maps on the finite products. They commute with each restriction and hence with the alternating differential; they also commute with theta componentwise. They therefore identify kernels and images and induce an additive equivalence on homology intertwining theta. Compose with the two edge isomorphisms and reindex small Ext through homAddEquiv, which commutes with postcomposition. All isomorphisms are chosen before theta. The empty cover and zero module yield zero complexes.

from.place: Proper-case proof: identify H^1(C,G_a) with H^1(C,O_C) compatibly with endomorphisms, before interpreting Frobenius-minus-identity on the finite-dimensional vector space. This node supplies the positive-degree coefficient-universe part of that comparison.

theorem exists_etaleTensorSectionsSheaf_cohomology_ulift_natural_succ
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [X.IsSeparated]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (n : ℕ) :
    let E := etaleTensorSectionsSheaf F
    let L := sheafCompose X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u}
    ∃ e : Sheaf.H (L.obj E) (n + 1) ≃+
        @Sheaf.H _ _ X.smallEtaleTopology E inferInstance (HasExt.standard _) (n + 1),
      ∀ (θ : E ⟶ E) (x : Sheaf.H (L.obj E) (n + 1)),
        e (Sheaf.H.map (L.map θ) (n + 1) x) =
          @Sheaf.H.map.{u + 1, u, u, u + 1} _ _ X.smallEtaleTopology
            inferInstance (HasExt.standard _)
            _ _ θ (n + 1) (e x)
